data_quote: [text, p. 515] Gill and McMahon (1986) reported that in *Banksia ornata*, a serotinous obligate seeder, common in parts of southern Australia, stand replacement may be likely after 16 years of age if post-fire emergence took place from 20% of available seeds. Seeds first become available at about 6 years in *B. ornata* (Gill & McMahon 1986), a figure comparable to that in *B. ericifolia* and *P. pulchella*.

data_location: abstract, p. 35; resprout flowering: text, p. 40; fire response: text, p. 42; fire response: text, p. 39; site: text, p. 36; fire: text, p. 36; rainfall after fire: text, p. 43
data_quote: [abstract, p. 35] No seedlings of *S. garlandii* flowered in their first summer, while 44% of the surviving 143 seedlings flowered in their second year and over 95% of the surviving 122 plants flowered in their third year.; [resprout flowering: text, p. 40] In their first year no seedlings in the quadrat flowered or had formed flower primordia, while the two rootstocks had finished flowering by late November but fruits had not been released.; [fire response: text, p. 42] This study indicates that *S. garlandii* is principally a seeder although some plants function as sprouters after a low-intensity fire.; [fire response: text, p. 39] While the fire killed many of the existing *Senecio* plants some survived by resprouting from a rootstock.; [site: text, p. 36] At only 340 ha, The Rock Nature Reserve (lat. 35° 16' S, long. 147° 05' E) is a small island of remnant native vegetation, surrounded by extensive agricultural lands.; [fire: text, p. 36] After less than 75 mm of rain during November 1990 to March 1991 (average 208 mm for this period) the first major fire (15–17 March 1991) in 40 years burnt more than 90% of The Rock Nature Reserve (personal observation).; [rainfall after fire: text, p. 43] This suggests that a low fire intensity, combined with more than the about 25 mm of rainfall received in the 2.5 months after the March fire (Fig. 2), then more *Senecio* rootstocks may have resprouted.
notes: age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3: no value printed as a time; no seedlings flowered in their first year, 44% of 143 surviving seedlings flowered in their second year and over 95% of 122 surviving plants in their third year, best reading 2 years; time to 50% and 80% flowering not stated (between second and third year); time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a: no value printed as a time; two rootstocks had finished flowering by late november of the first year after the march 1991 fire, best reading <1 year, n = 2; fire_response_categorical_surv1: printed 'principally a seeder although some plants function as sprouters', fire killed many plants, some survived by resprouting from a rootstock; p. 43: a specialised rootstock or similar organ does not appear to be present; fire_season_categorical derived from fire date 15-17 march 1991; fire_severity_categorical: 'low-intensity fire' on p. 42, also called the first major fire in 40 years; rainfall_post_fire_mm printed 'about 25 mm', from forest hill station about 35 km ne of the site; sample_size = surviving seedlings at the second-year flowering count
source: burrows, g. e. (1995). post-fire regeneration and growth of senecio garlandii (asteraceae) - a vulnerable plant of the south western slopes, nsw. cunninghamia, 4(1), 35-44.
